description.short: Brisk, iconic tea with a signature wintergreen and wine-like character, shaped by the region's unique desiccating monsoon winds
description.overview: The only region in Sri Lanka where warm, dry foehn-like monsoon winds blowing across eastern slopes in summer induce intense natural leaf stress, generating an unmistakable minty, brisk pungency.
description.aroma: Pungent, eucalyptus, wintergreen menthol, with sweet wine acidity
description.taste: Vibrant, brisk, with a signature cooling wintergreen snap and complex citrus acidity
description.processing: Plucking → rapid withering driven by dry mountain winds → orthodox rolling → full oxidation → drying

history.origin: Uva lies on the leeward eastern slopes of Sri Lanka's central massif, where dry katabatic winds accelerate natural leaf withering during specific months.
history.development: This seasonal microclimate creates a narrow window (July–September) when seasonal Uva develops its world-famous mentholated character.
history.modern: Uva is one of the three classic high-grown terroirs of Sri Lanka (alongside Nuwara Eliya and Dimbula), prized by blenders and single-estate collectors alike.
interestingFacts: Uva is among the few teas in the world whose iconic sensory signature depends strictly on a specific seasonal wind (the Cachan wind).
Only tea plucked during this meteorological window achieves true 'seasonal Uva' status; off-season pickings lack the distinctive menthol pungency.
